# **Clinical Trial Site Activation: Milestones, Dependencies, and Delays**

## **Overview**

Site activation is the work between a sponsor selecting a site and authorizing it to enroll patients, and it averages about seven months per site. Industry benchmarking from the Tufts Center for the Study of Drug Development finds start-up can take up to 30% of a trial's total timeline ([CASRAI](https://casrai.org/guides/study-start-up-clinical-trials)).

No single person owns the whole process. A sponsor or CRO associate tracks every site, while site teams handle the IRB, contracts, budget, pharmacy, training, and documents. Each handoff between these groups is a place where work stalls ([DRK Research](https://drkresearch.com/feeds/blog/clinical-trial-site-activation-process)), which is the gap TrialFlow targets.

## **Standard milestones**

Most sources describe the same core set of milestones, grouped into regulatory, contractual, and operational workstreams ([Advarra](https://www.advarra.com/resources/study-startup/), [ACRP](https://acrpnet.org/2026/02/17/improving-study-start-up-efficiency-to-accelerate-the-clinical-trial-timeline)). Exact checklists vary by protocol; device trials or trials without a pharmacy have shorter lists ([CASRAI SIV checklist](https://casrai.org/guides/site-initiation-visit-checklist)).

| Milestone | What it involves | Typical owner |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Feasibility and site selection | Site completes a feasibility questionnaire; sponsor may run a selection visit | Sponsor/CRO, site PI |
| IRB approval | Ethics review of the protocol, consent forms, and investigator | IRB, site regulatory staff |
| Contract executed | Clinical trial agreement covering responsibilities, indemnity, and IP rights | Site contracts office, sponsor legal |
| Budget finalized | Per-visit payments, start-up fees, and Medicare coverage analysis | Site finance, sponsor |
| Regulatory documents | FDA Form 1572, CVs, licenses, financial disclosures, delegation log | Site coordinator |
| Staff training | Good Clinical Practice plus protocol-specific training | Study team |
| Pharmacy setup | Secure, temperature-monitored storage and an accountability log | Research pharmacist |
| Lab and systems access | Lab kits, certifications, and data-capture system logins | Lab manager, coordinator |
| Drug (IP) shipped and received | Investigational product released, shipped, and logged at the site | Sponsor supply team, pharmacy |
| Site initiation visit (SIV) | Monitor's final readiness check of everything above | Sponsor CRA |
| Green light | Sponsor's written authorization to begin enrollment | Sponsor |

## **Dependencies**

Most workstreams run in parallel after selection, then converge on the SIV, which typically follows IRB approval and contract execution ([Mount Sinai](https://researchroadmap.mssm.edu/industry/site-initiation-visit/)). Good Clinical Practice guidance requires IRB and regulatory approval before drug is supplied ([AQ Trials](https://aq-trials.com/trial-pharmacy-green-light-siv/)), and green light comes only after every gating SIV action item is closed ([CASRAI](https://casrai.org/guides/site-initiation-visit-checklist)).

![][image1]

Contract and budget negotiation run side by side, and both must clear before activation, so a delay in either one pushes back the green light.

## **Typical timelines and delays**

Contracts and IRB review are the two most-cited bottlenecks, and the early stages (selection through contract execution) take the longest and vary the most between sites ([CASRAI](https://casrai.org/guides/study-start-up-clinical-trials)). Benchmarks depend on where the clock starts, so treat these as ranges, not standards.

| Measure | Reported figure | Source |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Pre-study visit to first patient | 6.5 months (Phase I); 10.4 months (Phase II–IV) | Tufts CSDD, via [DRK Research](https://drkresearch.com/feeds/blog/clinical-trial-startup-timeline) |
| Cancer center trial activation | 167-day median (2018 survey); NCI target is 90 days | [Applied Clinical Trials](https://www.appliedclinicaltrialsonline.com/view/accelerating-clinical-trial-activation) |
| US IRB review | About 1 week exempt, 2–4 weeks expedited, 4–6 weeks full board | WCG 2024, via [DRK Research](https://drkresearch.com/feeds/blog/clinical-trial-site-activation-process) |
| Central vs. local IRB | 27 vs. 66 days in one analysis | [DRK Research](https://drkresearch.com/feeds/blog/clinical-trial-startup-timeline) |
| Contract negotiation | 39 days with standard templates vs. 73 days custom | CTSA study, via [DRK Research](https://drkresearch.com/feeds/blog/clinical-trial-startup-timeline) |

The recurring causes of delay are:

* **Contract and budget negotiation.** Disputes over payments, indemnification, or IP rights, and budgets that miss work in the protocol ([Umbrex](https://umbrex.com/resources/life-science-industry-playbooks/clinical-trial-start-up-playbook/contracts-budgets-and-site-negotiation/)).  
* **Incomplete documentation.** Missing forms, outdated CVs, or incomplete IRB packets trigger extra review cycles ([ACRP](https://acrpnet.org/2026/02/17/improving-study-start-up-efficiency-to-accelerate-the-clinical-trial-timeline)).  
* **Sequential instead of parallel work.** Waiting for IRB approval before starting contracts adds the two timelines together ([CASRAI](https://casrai.org/guides/study-start-up-clinical-trials)).  
* **No clear owner or tracking.** Stalled items sit for weeks without follow-up or escalation ([DRK Research](https://drkresearch.com/feeds/blog/clinical-trial-site-activation-process)).  
* **"Ready on paper" gaps.** A contract may be signed while training is incomplete, or drug released but not yet received by the pharmacy ([Umbrex](https://umbrex.com/resources/life-science-industry-playbooks/clinical-trial-start-up-playbook/site-activation-greenlight-and-first-patient-in/)).

## **Implications for TrialFlow**

The research supports modeling each site as about 11 milestones across parallel workstreams, gated by the SIV and green light. Concretely:

* **Task template.** Use the milestones table above as the default template, with a "not applicable" status for trials without a drug or pharmacy component.  
* **Dependencies.** Encode the gates shown in the diagram: IRB approval and pharmacy setup before drug shipment, everything before the SIV, and the SIV before green light.  
* **Schema fields.** Beyond owner, status, and dates, track "days in current status" and "activation impact" (none, at risk, blocking), which mirror fields real contract trackers use ([Umbrex](https://umbrex.com/resources/life-science-industry-playbooks/clinical-trial-start-up-playbook/contracts-budgets-and-site-negotiation/)).  
* **Synthetic data.** Draw task durations from the benchmark ranges above, and inject most delays into contracts, budgets, and IRB review so the scenarios match real-world patterns.  
* **Open question for a domain expert.** Do sponsors usually require an executed contract before releasing drug to a site, in addition to IRB approval?
